agent_summary: CVE-2024-43373 is an arbitrary file write in the npm 'webcrack' module (<=2.14.0) via path traversal using Windows path separators (backslash). The vulnerable behavior is specific to Windows: webcrack applies node:path POSIX normalize/join, which do not treat '\' as a separator, so the modulePath.startsWith(path) check is bypassed while the native writeFile later decodes '\' as a separator on Windows. On Linux, backslash is an ordinary filename character, so the same malicious bundle does not traverse and no arbitrary file write occurs. The upstream fix commit (4bc5c6f) guards its Windows regression test with test.runIf(sep === '\\'), confirming only Windows is affected. Because the affected behavior is Windows-specific and not reproducible on a Linux NixOS VM, the CVE is out of scope for the NICE Archive (Linux) framework per the eligibility gate. No case directory or reproduction was created.
failure_reason: Out of scope: arbitrary-file-write vulnerability is specific to Windows (backslash path separators)
worktree: the Linux build of webcrack is not affected by the same behavior and it cannot be demonstrated in a Linux NixOS VM.
